forcedChoices.reason: The packet asks for the first word in capitals; Spanish needs the article, so only the article is in capitals.
The English coins 'scapeman' on 'scapegoat'; the Spanish pairs it with 'chivo expiatorio' to keep the same echo without a note.
Spanish has no plain 'unholy' for objects; 'profano' gives 'not holy' and avoids the moral sense of 'impío'.
'prayers' here means people who pray, not prayers; 'orantes' carries that sense.
'tortas' means a sandwich in Mexico and 'pasteles' reads as dessert; 'panecillos' keeps small baked cakes neutral.
'sense' and 'feeling' are separate words in the English; 'sensación' and 'sentimiento' keep both, and 'sensación de culpa' stays in 89:10.4.
The text speaks to the reader in the plural; the packet asks for 'ustedes'.
